notes: Chunk A = module M1 (fractals, book section 4.1, pdf pages 1 to 6), 13 units, 20 items.
Required: the three 'draw the initial steps' solutions (carpet C7, gasket C12, Koch C19) and the worked example on the midpoints of an equilateral triangle (C8). Everything else is text/LaTeX.
All three 'draw the steps' questions are none on the question side (no given figure) and required on the solution side: same decision across the set.

The four Figure it Out questions Q2/Q3 (units 7, 8, 12, 13) have formula answers, so none/none; their LP book_number says 'Figure it Out, Q1' for all four, which is wrong (they are Q2, Q3 of the triangle and of the snowflake).
The solution figures use MARK_FILL for the remaining pieces and ANSWER green for the count tags (no question diagram exists to derive from).
Weakest required item: C8 (midpoints worked example); a reviewer who prefers text only can flip it to none without touching the others.
Counts match the LP solution text, and were recomputed: carpet squares 1, 8, 64 and holes 0, 1, 9; gasket triangles 1, 3, 9 and holes 0, 1, 4; Koch sides 3, 12, 48.

diagram.manim_description: Canvas 16 by 8 units (2:1, 1920 x 960 px), plain BG white; 1 unit = 120 px. Draw three squares of side 4 units in one row, left to right, with their lower-left corners at (1,3), (6,3) and (11,3), so every square spans y = 3 to y = 7. Remaining squares are filled MARK_FILL; a hole is BG white; every outline is INK. Square 1 (Step 0): one solid square, MARK_FILL, 3 px INK outline, no inner lines, no hole. Square 2 (Step 1): cut into a 3 by 3 grid of cells of side 1.3333 (cells counted as (row, column) from 1, row 1 at the top, column 1 at the left). The cell (2,2) is the hole, BG white; the other 8 cells are MARK_FILL; every cell has a 2 px INK outline. Square 3 (Step 2): cut into a 9 by 9 grid of cells of side 0.4444. The 3 by 3 block of cells in rows 4 to 6 and columns 4 to 6 is ONE white hole of side 1.3333 with a single 2 px INK outline and no inner lines. Eight single cells are white holes: (2,2), (2,5), (2,8), (5,2), (5,8), (8,2), (8,5), (8,8). The remaining 64 cells are MARK_FILL with a 2 px INK outline. Under each square, centred on the square, write in INK at y = 2.3 the text 'Step 0', 'Step 1', 'Step 2' (x = 3, 8, 13), then in ANSWER green two lines of text, the first at y = 1.5 and the second at y = 0.8: under Step 0 '1 square' and '0 holes'; under Step 1 '8 squares' and '1 hole'; under Step 2 '64 squares' and '9 holes'. Text height 0.45 unit (54 px), sans-serif. Nothing else is drawn.
must_not_show: inner lines inside a white hole
accuracy_checks: squares of the 3 steps: 1, 8, 64 = 8^0, 8^1, 8^2 (Step 2 has 81 cells - 9 in the big hole - 8 single holes = 64 remaining)
holes: 0, 1, 1 + 8 = 9 (Step 2: 1 big hole of side 4/3 plus 8 single-cell holes of side 4/9)
the 8 single-cell holes are the centre cells of the 8 outer 3 by 3 blocks of the 9 by 9 grid

diagram.manim_description: Canvas 10 by 10 units (1:1, 1920 x 1920 px), plain BG white. Draw an equilateral triangle of side 8 units, apex up, horizontal base, 3 px INK outline, no fill: lower-left vertex (1,1.9), lower-right vertex (9,1.9), top vertex (5,8.8282). Mark the midpoint of each side with a small filled INK dot of radius 0.1: (5,1.9) on the bottom side, (3,5.3641) on the left side, (7,5.3641) on the right side. Join the three midpoints with three straight 3 px INK segments: (3,5.3641) to (7,5.3641), (3,5.3641) to (5,1.9), (7,5.3641) to (5,1.9). This cuts the triangle into four triangles, each with sides of 4 units, drawn without fill and without any marks inside them. Write '8 cm' in INK, height 0.5 unit (60 px), centred below the bottom side at (5,1.1). No vertex letters, no angle marks and no other labels.
must_not_show: shading or colours inside the four triangles
accuracy_checks: the three dots are the midpoints of the three sides: (5,1.9), (3,5.3641), (7,5.3641)
each joining segment is 4 units, so the four triangles each have sides of 4 units
the figure shows only what the question gives (side 8 cm, midpoints joined), not the 4 cm or 60 degrees of the solution
diagram.alt_text: An equilateral triangle with side 8 cm; the midpoints of its three sides are joined, cutting it into four triangles.
